title: VetLab Bridge: veterinary diagnostics results interchange for independent labs and the long tail

problem_severity_frequency.rationale: Manual re-entry or PDF attachment of lab results is practitioner-evidenced, though frequency and population are not quantified by any cited source.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: The hypothesised payer is the independent lab, but no evidence shows labs funding a results-delivery channel; labs are small and price-sensitive. Inferred buyer only.

evidence_strength.rationale: Sources are one vendor-authored analysis, one practitioner model, one non-replicated paper and vendor pages; vendor claims are weak secondary and do not establish demand. No primary buyer-side evidence.

distribution.rationale: A small lab population allows direct outreach and open PIMS programmes are plausible channels, but no lab is named and no partner interest is evidenced.

differentiation.rationale: Capped at 2: direct incumbent overlap. ManuCare already markets universal lab-result import and DataHub Vet normalises PIMS data; the wedge is a feature of the integration category.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: A desk capability check is cheap; an outright buyer interview programme is untested and was never run, so this cannot score above 3.

feasibility.rationale: Technically feasible (middleware and sidecars already do parts of it) but hard: per-PIMS connectors, per-lab mappings and access-fee constraints.

economics.rationale: Capped at 2: modelled only. A low ACV must clear a documented $30-50/clinic/month access-fee floor.

founder_fit.rationale: No source about who would found or sell this; null per method/scorecard.md (no source, no score).

risk.rationale: Animal clinical data falls outside GDPR, but processor obligations for attached owner data and connector/contract exposure were not assessed, so risk is moderate rather than low.

economic_buyer.note: Independent labs are the hypothesised payer, but no evidence shows them funding a results channel and they are small and price-sensitive.
economic_buyer.resolve_via: Interview 5 independent/regional UK/IE vet labs about who would fund a results bridge and at what per-practice price.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: Manual re-entry/attachment of results is practitioner-evidenced; frequency and budget are not quantified.

non_paid_distribution.note: A small, nameable lab population and open PIMS programmes make unpaid outreach plausible but untested.
non_paid_distribution.resolve_via: Test whether 10 named independent labs and 20 practices respond to direct outreach without paid acquisition.

defensible_wedge.note: ManuCare already markets universal CSV/HL7 lab-result import into the patient case ('zero copy-paste') and DataHub Vet already exposes a normalised veterinary data model into six long-tail PIMS. Under method/scorecard.md a wedge that is a feature of an established category is a hard-filter failure. Data migration of this kind is not a durable asset for a new entrant.

no_network_effects_needed.note: One lab plus one practice derives value from a single structured results channel; no network is required for first value.

plausible_margins.note: A low ACV must clear a documented $30-50/clinic/month access-fee floor; not modelled with a real price.
plausible_margins.resolve_via: Model per-lab and per-practice pricing against the access-fee floor with a partner PIMS.

acceptable_risk.note: Processor obligations where owner personal data travels with results, and the contractual exposure of an unsanctioned local connection, were not assessed.
acceptable_risk.resolve_via: Obtain a legal/privacy view on processor obligations and connector terms before any pilot.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: A desk capability check of ManuCare, DataHub Vet and the IDEXX/Covetrus bundles is cheap and decisive about the wedge.

not_all_optimistic.note: Buyer, wedge and margin would all have to resolve favourably at once, and the wedge is already contradicted by a shipping product.
